rv.q: Moss and Jamie Armitage’s infectiously fun production is packed with witty touches that make history, and theatre, easily accessible.
Anne Boleyn, Jane Seymour and co tell their stories in a lively new musical that makes serious points about how women are eras…
You'd need a heart of stone to resist.
This may be feminism-lite, but it ignites powerful passions.
Iconic? Yes, absolutely – just in more ways than one.
But if this is the future of feminism, lop my head off now.
This is a unique, exciting, and fun show that can be consumed repeatedly.
Indeed, no matter how many of the previous casts you’ve seen, this is the line-up you don’t want to miss.
If you are looking for a highly entertaining, music filled night at the theatre I would 100% recommend this show to you.
The franticness of Six won't win over everybody, but the skill of Marlow and Moss' songwriting, and the musicals' showcasing of acting talent, demonstrates the grit beneath the glitz.
Catchy music, funny jokes, but an ultimately forgettable performance.
